titleEn: Sabanto and Verdant Robotics integrate autonomy and precision application systems
titleZh: Sabanto与Verdant Robotics整合自动驾驶与精准施药系统
summaryZh: 美国两家公司Sabanto Inc.和Verdant Robotics首次完成系统集成，将Sabanto的拖拉机自动驾驶系统与Verdant的SharpShooter精准施药系统结合，实现从田间导航到植株级施药的全程无人化作业。该集成方案已在佛罗里达州Bethel Farms的草皮生产中投入商业运营，累计作业超9900英亩，可显著降低投入成本并缓解劳动力短缺问题。
featuredReason: 该集成代表了农机自动驾驶与植株级精准施药两大前沿技术的深度融合，为智慧农业中"无人化田间作业"提供了可落地的商业案例，对畜牧行业中的饲草种植和田间管理同样具有参考价值。

Photos: Sabanto A Sabanto-equipped autonomous tractor pulls a Verdant Robotics SharpShooter unit through a field, running without an operator in the cab. Photos: Sabanto U.S. companies Sabanto Inc. and Verdant Robotics have integrated their systems for the first time, enabling producers to automate field work from navigation to plant-level input application without an operator in the cab. The integration connects Sabanto’s Autonomy System with Verdant Robotics’ SharpShooter precision application system. SharpShooter, which uses Aim & Apply technology to identify individual plants and weeds and apply inputs only where needed, now runs behind Sabanto-equipped autonomous tractors. According to the companies, the two systems now function as a single, integrated solution. The tractor handles navigation and powers the implement, while SharpShooter communicates directly with the Sabanto-equipped tractor through the CAN bus, feeding real-time field data to the Sabanto Autonomy System during active navigation. Based on that data, SharpShooter directs the tractor to adjust speed and implement height according to field conditions. Sabanto says the combined system autonomously executes decisions that would previously have required a skilled operator in the cab. The integration is already running in commercial operations across various crop markets, including sod production at Bethel Farms in Arcadia, Florida. Bethel Farms, a family-owned sod, citrus and grass plug grower, has worked over 9,900 acres using Sabanto’s autonomy system. The company says the combined system is demonstrating reliable performance in demanding field conditions. !Image 7: Close-up of the SharpShooter's Aim & Apply system as it targets individual plants and weeds during a field pass. Close-up of the SharpShooter's Aim & Apply system as it targets individual plants and weeds during a field pass. Cutting input costs “Our goal has always been to make full autonomy accessible and immediately valuable for everyone in the ag industry – farmers, implement providers, retailers, input providers, and tractor manufacturers alike”, says Craig Rupp, Founder and CEO of Sabanto. “By pairing our retrofit autonomy system with Verdant’s technology, we’re giving producers and stakeholders a complete solution that works on their existing equipment. Farmers can run precision operations 247, addressing labour shortages head-on while dramatically cutting input costs.” “Growers invested in SharpShooter to reduce inputs, run operations their crews can’t always staff, and take back control of their application window,” emphasises Gabe Sibley, Co-Founder and CEO of Verdant Robotics. “This integration means they can do all of that without an operator in the cab – more acres covered, fewer people required, and the same plant-level precision on every pass.” !Image 8: The Sabanto Autonomy System's GNSS and camera hardware mounted on a retrofitted tractor. The Sabanto Autonomy System's GNSS and camera hardware mounted on a retrofitted tractor. Retrofit compatibility Sabanto’s autonomy system combines high-precision GNSS, cameras, an advanced vehicle operating system and proprietary path-planning. The integration with SharpShooter is compatible across a wide range of tractor makes and models, in line with Sabanto’s retrofit philosophy of using farmers’ existing equipment. Sabanto is headquartered in Ames, Iowa, with operations in Itasca, Illinois. The company builds aftermarket retrofit kits that convert existing tractors into fully autonomous machines. Verdant Robotics, headquartered in Hayward, California, develops precision application technology for weeding, thinning and input delivery with millimetre-level accuracy. Its SharpShooter system uses what the company describes as physical AI to aim before applying inputs, targeting individual plants and weeds. translationZh:
美国公司Sabanto Inc.和Verdant Robotics首次完成系统集成，使生产者能够在无驾驶员在驾驶室的情况下，实现从田间导航到植株级投入品施用的全程自动化作业。

该集成将Sabanto的自动驾驶系统与Verdant Robotics的SharpShooter精准施药系统连接起来。SharpShooter采用“瞄准与施用”（Aim & Apply）技术，能够识别单株作物和杂草，仅在需要的位置施用投入品，如今该设备可挂接在配备Sabanto系统的自动驾驶拖拉机后方运行。

据两家公司介绍，这两套系统现已作为一个集成解决方案协同工作。拖拉机负责导航并为农具提供动力，而SharpShooter通过CAN总线直接与配备Sabanto系统的拖拉机通信，在主动导航过程中将实时田间数据反馈给Sabanto自动驾驶系统。基于这些数据，SharpShooter引导拖拉机根据田间状况调整行驶速度和农具高度。

Sabanto表示，这套组合系统能够自主执行以往需要驾驶室内有经验驾驶员才能完成的决策。该集成已在美国多个作物市场的商业运营中投入使用，包括佛罗里达州阿卡迪亚的Bethel Farms草皮生产。Bethel Farms是一家家族经营的草皮、柑橘和草种苗种植企业，已使用Sabanto自动驾驶系统作业超过9900英亩。该公司表示，这套组合系统在严苛的田间条件下表现出可靠的性能。

**降低投入成本**

“我们的目标一直是让完全自动驾驶变得易于获取，并为农业行业中的每个人——农民、农具供应商、零售商、投入品供应商和拖拉机制造商——立即创造价值，”Sabanto创始人兼首席执行官Craig Rupp表示。“通过将我们的后装式自动驾驶系统与Verdant的技术配对，我们为生产者和利益相关方提供了一套可在现有设备上运行的完整解决方案。农民可以全天候运行精准作业，直接应对劳动力短缺问题，同时大幅降低投入成本。”

“投资SharpShooter的种植者希望减少投入品使用、完成团队无法始终配备人手的作业，并重新掌控施药窗口期，”Verdant Robotics联合创始人兼首席执行官Gabe Sibley强调。“这次集成意味着他们可以在没有驾驶员在驾驶室的情况下实现所有这些目标——覆盖更多英亩、需要更少人员，并且在每次作业中保持同样的植株级精准度。”

**后装兼容性**

Sabanto的自动驾驶系统结合了高精度GNSS、摄像头、先进的车辆操作系统和专有路径规划技术。与SharpShooter的集成兼容多种拖拉机品牌和型号，符合Sabanto利用农民现有设备进行后装改造的理念。

Sabanto总部位于爱荷华州埃姆斯，在伊利诺伊州伊塔斯卡设有运营机构。该公司制造后市场改装套件，可将现有拖拉机改装为完全自动驾驶的机器。Verdant Robotics总部位于加利福尼亚州海沃德，开发用于除草、间苗和投入品施用的精准施药技术，精度达到毫米级。其SharpShooter系统采用该公司所称的“物理人工智能”（physical AI），在施用前进行瞄准，针对单株作物和杂草进行精准作业。
contentHtml: U.S. companies Sabanto Inc. and Verdant Robotics have integrated their systems for the first time, enabling producers to automate field work from navigation to plant-level input application without an operator in the cab.
